title: The backbone configuration file
description: A backbone file schema (ADR-056): the project's declarations to the backbone, kept in one project-owned file at `.pkit/project/config.yaml` (COR-048 point 1). Every key is owned by a core record, which defines its meaning, its default and who may write it (COR-048 point 2); an absent file, an empty file or a missing key means the owning record's default applies (point 3). Validation is strict: an unknown key is an error carrying the nearest known key, rendered by `project_kit.backbone_schemas`; commands that merely read the file must never fail because of it and use the default (point 4). The reserved `project` block is checked only for being well-formed. Bound by its fixed path, never by a field. Backbone-owned; carries no version of its own and is migrated when it changes (COR-010, ADR-056 point 3).

name.description: The project's declared name, rendered wherever the backbone names the project (COR-048 point 2, first entry). Declared here so it is never derived from a folder or remote name. Default: none — readers fall back to the git remote's repository name.

project.title: The reserved `project` block (COR-048 point 2)
project.description: Keys owned by the project's own decision records. Checked only for being well-formed — a mapping — and otherwise not inspected; project-supplied schemas for it are deferred until a real need appears.

docs.title: Documentation roots, by audience (COR-049)
docs.description: Where the project's documentation lives. Each root is a directory path relative to the repository root whose resolved location, after following links, lies inside the repository and outside the methodology's own tree (`.pkit/`); validation checks that and warns when the directory does not exist yet (COR-049 points 1 and 7). The two roots may be the same folder, or one nested in the other. Both default to `docs/`.

user.description: The user root: where user-facing documentation (how to use the system) lives. Default `docs/`. No backbone consumer today; components that place user-facing documents derive from it.

internal.description: The internal root: where technical documentation for maintainers and agents (decisions, architecture, contributing and release guides, analysis) lives. Default `docs/`. Components that choose a documentation location derive it from this root plus their conventional sub-path (COR-049 point 4).

friction.title: Friction settings (COR-050 point 14)
friction.description: The project's settings for anchors and friction, named for the functionality and its command group. Every path here stays inside the repository (validation refuses one that does not) and a pattern matching nothing is a warning (a dead pattern would keep silence looking like health).

mode.description: How the change check treats what it finds (COR-050 point 12): `warning` reports and passes; `enforcing` fails on friction, dead anchors and a bump with nothing behind it. Default `warning`. An invalid value is a validation error, so enforcement is never switched off silently.

status-job.description: When the job that writes the tool-written `last-check` status runs (COR-050 point 10): `never`, or `after-merge` — after each merge to the project's default branch. Default `never`.

places.description: The project's own anchored places: paths or globs, relative to the repository root, where the friction check looks for artefacts carrying the methodology's container (COR-050 point 1). `**` matches across folders. Default: none. Components declare their places in their own package metadata, not here.

surface.description: The project's declared surface: paths or globs, relative to the repository root, that artefacts are expected to anchor to; the check reports the uncovered part (COR-050 point 14). Default: none.

exclude.description: Paths or globs, relative to the repository root, that the friction checks leave out. Default: none.

connections.title: Connection selections (COR-053 point 7, COR-052 point 4)
connections.description: The project's answers to wiring conflicts, in the block named for the functionality. Empty by default; written with consent by configuration commands or when a conflict is reported; validated against what is installed; cleared on uninstall with consent (COR-048 point 2, 'keys naming installed components').

providers.title: The provider-selection key
providers.description: Selects one capability per qualified role: a mapping from `<publisher>::<role>` to the name of the installed capability that answers the role. Validation checks that the capability is installed; that it provides the role is checked once package metadata declares roles.

selections.title: The contributor-selection key
selections.description: Selects one contributor per `single` data point when several capabilities contribute to it: a mapping from `<publisher>::<role>:<point>` to the name of the installed capability whose contribution wins (COR-052 point 4 with COR-053's role-qualified address). Validation checks that the capability is installed; that the point is a declared `single` point the capability fills is checked once package metadata declares points.

process.title: Process settings (COR-033 point 7)
process.description: The project's settings for the process engine, in the block named for the functionality.

journal.title: Journal logging (COR-033 point 7)
journal.description: Whether the process engine keeps an append-only, per-subject journal of the moves it validates and executes — optional audit, never the source of truth: position is always re-derived from reality, so no verdict depends on it. Written by the project (by hand, or `pkit config set`) and by the upgrade migration that introduced the key, which records logging as on for a project that already kept journals.

enabled.description: Keep the journal. Default `false`: the engine writes and reads no journal, and the commands that show history say journal logging is not enabled.

committed.description: When logging is on, whether the journals are committed with the project (`true` — shared, reviewable, kept across clones) or kept local to each clone and ignored by version control (`false`). The rendered `.pkit/.gitignore` follows it. Default `false`; without `enabled` it has no effect and journals stay ignored.

repository.title: Repository facts (COR-054)
repository.description: Facts about the repository that every reader takes from one place.

default-branch.description: The branch the project's settled work lands on — declared once, for every reader (COR-054 point 1). Resolved as the remote-tracking reference `origin/<name>` when it names a commit, else the local branch `<name>` (point 2); a comparison's base named for one run (`--base`, `$PKIT_CHECK_BASE`) replaces it for that run only (point 3). A branch name: no whitespace, not starting with `-`. Default `main`. Written by the project, by hand or `pkit config set`.

capability-name.description: The name of an installed capability, as registered in `.pkit/manifest.yaml`.

repo-relative-directory.description: A directory path relative to the repository root. Not absolute; a trailing slash is allowed.

repo-relative-patterns.description: Paths or globs relative to the repository root; `**` matches across folders. Not absolute.
